output.title: Credential rotation is a workflow cost, not just a security topic
output.body:
If you run a small business, credential rotation usually shows up as a workflow problem before it looks like a security one. An API key gets changed, a SaaS login expires, or access is moved, and then somebody has to re-enter details by hand before the integration works again. The cost is not abstract. It is the time spent noticing the break, tracing which account changed, and fixing the follow-on mess.

This is also one of those cases where AI is not the main question. Credential rotation is mostly a systems and access-management issue, not a judgment task. AI can sit around it, for example by helping route alerts or document what changed, but the owner decision is still about how credentials are stored, updated, and checked. If the process is loose, better software will not magically tidy it up.

The practical next step is simple: list the integrations and accounts you manually manage today, then count how often someone re-enters or updates a credential in a month. Pick one recent failure and write down how long it took to notice and repair. That gives you a real baseline for comparing manual work, tooling, or hiring. Until you know that number, you are guessing in a very polite way.
